obtained.how: abstract only: Crossref's record of the DOI (the publisher's abstract); the article is subscriber-only at Oxford University Press (formerly T&F), and no repository or author copy was found

bibliography.note: Huff, David D.; Grad, Gabriella; Williamson, Craig E. 2004. Environmental constraints on spawning depth of yellow perch: the roles of low temperature and high solar ultraviolet radiation. Transactions of the American Fisheries Society 133(3): 718–726.

claims.claim: in a low-DOC Pennsylvania lake ~92 % of perch eggs lay deeper than 3 m and UV at the surface killed all eggs, whereas in a higher-DOC lake 76 % lay shallower than 1 m (abstract)
claims.note: No full text. The abstract states all three: 92 % of eggs in the low-DOC lake deeper than 3 m, 'UVR in the surface waters of the low-DOC lake killed 100% of the eggs before hatching', and 76 % of eggs in the higher-DOC lake in water less than 1 m deep. The paper correctly labels it 'abstract'.

claims.claim: yellow perch spawn in brown water mostly < 1 m (Huff, Grad & Williamson 2004, abstract)
claims.note: The abstract gives 76 % of eggs < 1 m in the 'higher-DOC' lake; it does not call that lake brown or give its DOC (the notes' 'DOC 4.7 mg/L, Lake Lacawac' needs the full text).

claims.claim: yellow perch eggs near the surface of a Pennsylvania lake hatched in 9 days at a mean 13.3 °C, while deeper eggs at 7.7–11 °C took 19–35 days (Huff et al. 2004, abstract)
claims.note: These numbers are NOT in the abstract, which says only that surface eggs in the higher-DOC lake hatched '10–26 d shorter' than surface eggs in the low-DOC lake or deeper eggs in the higher-DOC lake. The '(abstract)' label is therefore wrong; the 9 d, 13.3 °C, 7.7–11 °C and 19–35 d came from somewhere else (the note egg_stage.md marks them [abstract], probably a search summary). Hold them until the full text is read, or reduce the sentence to the abstract's '10–26 d shorter'.
